items.plain: D-Link DIR-600L routers let a remote attacker run code on the device without logging in; disconnect or replace affected routers.
items.summary: A stack-based buffer overflow in the DIR-600L's authentication.cgi lets a remote, unauthenticated attacker run arbitrary code by manipulating the id and password parameters; the exploit is now public. Affects firmware 2.17 / 2.17b02 — disconnect or replace affected routers, as no vendor fix is listed.

items.plain: TRENDnet TEW-657BRM routers let a remote attacker crash or take over the device; the model is long out of support, so replace it.
items.summary: An out-of-bounds write in the TEW-657BRM's mini_httpd setup.cgi can be triggered remotely without authentication, and the exploit has been disclosed publicly. TRENDnet says the router has been end-of-life for over 15 years, so no patch is expected — replace the device.

items.plain: FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer let an attacker without a login run commands on the system; apply Fortinet's November patches now.
items.summary: Improper output encoding in the JSON-RPC API of FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer lets an unauthenticated attacker execute unauthorized code via a specially crafted HTTP request. Fortinet's November patch batch fixes it — upgrade FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer 8.0.x and 7.6.x.

items.plain: Red Hat Quay lets an attacker without a login forge access to private container images; upgrade Quay to a fixed release.
items.summary: An unauthenticated attacker can obtain an anonymous registry token, present it to Quay's service-key rotation endpoint, and install their own signing key with no expiry — then read and write any private repository and replace tags. Red Hat has released fixed Quay versions for all affected branches.

items.plain: ASP.NET Core lets a logged-in attacker send messages as another user inside SignalR apps; update .NET to the patched release.
items.summary: SignalR connections in ASP.NET Core are not consistently bound to the identity negotiated at connection setup, so an authorized attacker can inject messages that execute Hub invocations as the victim. Microsoft's November .NET update fixes it — upgrade to 8.0.34, 9.0.23, 10.0.15 or 11.0.0.
